p0.original: When the stock which a man possesses is no more than sufficient to maintain him for a few days or a few weeks, he seldom thinks of deriving any revenue from it. He consumes it as sparingly as he can, and endeavours, by his labour, to acquire something which may supply its place before it be consumed altogether. His revenue is, in this case, derived from his labour only. This is the state of the greater part of the labouring poor in all countries.
p0.zh: 当一个人拥有的股票不足以维持他几天或几个星期时,他很少考虑从中获取任何收入。 他尽其所能地消耗它,并努力通过自己的努力,在完全消耗之前,获得一些可能供应其位置的东西。 在这种情况下,他的收入只来自他的劳动。 这是所有国家中大部分贫困劳动者的状况。

p1.original: But when he possesses stock sufficient to maintain him for months or years, he naturally endeavours to derive a revenue from the greater part of it, reserving only so much for his immediate consumption as may maintain him till this revenue begins to come in. His whole stock, therefore, is distinguished into two parts. That part which he expects is to afford him this revenue is called his capital. The other is that which supplies his immediate consumption, and which consists either, first, in that portion of his whole stock which was originally reserved for this purpose; or, secondly, in his revenue, from whatever source derived, as it gradually comes in; or, thirdly, in such things as had been purchased by either of these in former years, and which are not yet entirely consumed, such as a stock of clothes, household furniture, and the like. In one or other, or all of these three articles, consists the stock which men commonly reserve for their own immediate consumption.
p1.zh: 但是,当他拥有足以维持他数月或数年的库存时,他自然会努力从大部分的库存中获取收入,只为他的即时消费预留了足够多的资金,直到这些收入开始出现为止。 因此,他的整个股票分为两部分。 他所期望的那部分是给他支付这笔收入,叫做他的资本。另一种是供应他即时消费的,包括:第一,他原先为此目的保留的全部库存中的那部分;第二,他的收入中,随着它逐渐进入,来自任何来源;第三,在他们中任何一个在前年购买过、但尚未完全消费的东西中,例如一套衣服、家俱等等。 在一条或另一条,或这三条的所有条款中,都包含男子通常为自己的即时消费而储备的库存。

p2.original: There are two different ways in which a capital may be employed so as to yield a revenue or profit to its employer.
p2.zh: 使用资本可以有两种不同的方式,以便给雇主带来收入或利润。

p3.original: First, it maybe employed in raising, manufacturing, or purchasing goods, and selling them again with a profit. The capital employed in this manner yields no revenue or profit to its employer, while it either remains in his possession, or continues in the same shape. The goods of the merchant yield him no revenue or profit till he sells them for money, and the money yields him as little till it is again exchanged for goods. His capital is continually going from him in one shape, and returning to him in another; and it is only by means of such circulation, or successive changes, that it can yield him any profit. Such capitals, therefore, may very properly be called circulating capitals.
p3.zh: 首先,它可能受雇于饲养、制造或购买商品,并再次以利润出售商品。以这种方式雇用的资本不会给雇主带来任何收入或利润,而这种资本要么仍由雇主拥有,要么继续以同样形式存在。商人的商品在他为了钱而卖掉之前,没有给他任何收入或利润,而这种商品在再次换货之前,他得到的也很少。 他的国库,不断从他那里流出,又以另一种形式返回他那里;只有这种流通,或不断的变更,才能使他获得任何利益。 因此,这种首都可以非常恰当地称为流通首都。

p4.original: Secondly, it may be employed in the improvement of land, in the purchase of useful machines and instruments of trade, or in such like things as yield a revenue or profit without changing masters, or circulating any further. Such capitals, therefore, may very properly be called fixed capitals.
p4.zh: 第二,它可用于改善土地,购买有用的机器和贸易工具,或者在不改变主人的情况下产生收入或利润,或进一步流通。 因此,这些首都可以非常恰当地称为固定首都。

p5.original: Different occupations require very different proportions between the fixed and circulating capitals employed in them.
p5.zh: 不同的职业要求所雇用的固定首都和流通首都的比例大不相同。

p6.original: The capital of a merchant, for example, is altogether a circulating capital. He has occasion for no machines or instruments of trade, unless his shop or warehouse be considered as such.
p6.zh: 例如,商人的首都完全是一个流通的首都。 除非他的商店或仓库被视为交易机器或工具,否则他没有机会从事交易。

p7.original: Some part of the capital of every master artificer or manufacturer must be fixed in the instruments of his trade. This part, however, is very small in some, and very great in others, A master tailor requires no other instruments of trade but a parcel of needles. Those of the master shoemaker are a little, though but a very little, more expensive. Those of the weaver rise a good deal above those of the shoemaker. The far greater part of the capital of all such master artificers, however, is circulated either in the wages of their workmen, or in the price of their materials, and repaid, with a profit, by the price of the work.
p7.zh: 每个工艺大师或制造商的部分资本必须固定在他的贸易工具中。 然而,这一部分在有些地方非常小,在另一些地方非常大,一个主裁缝不需要其他贸易工具,而需要一包针头。鞋师傅的鞋匠虽然有点,但价格也比较低廉. 那些织女们比鞋匠们的 高得多 然而,所有这类工艺大师的资本中,很大一部分不是以工人的工资,就是以材料的价格流通,而以利润的方式以工程的价格偿还。

p8.original: In other works a much greater fixed capital is required. In a great iron-work, for example, the furnace for melting the ore, the forge, the slit-mill, are instruments of trade which cannot be erected without a very great expense. In coal works, and mines of every kind, the machinery necessary, both for drawing out the water, and for other purposes, is frequently still more expensive.
p8.zh: 在其他工程中,需要更大的固定资本。 例如,在一个伟大的铁器工程中,熔化矿石的炉子、铸造、切割机是贸易工具,没有非常大的费用是无法建造的。 在煤炭工程和各种矿井中,抽水和其他用途所需的机械往往仍然比较昂贵。

p9.original: That part of the capital of the farmer which is employed in the instruments of agriculture is a fixed, that which is employed in the wages and maintenance of his labouring servants is a circulating capital. He makes a profit of the one by keeping it in his own possession, and of the other by parting with it. The price or value of his labouring cattle is a fixed capital, in the same manner as that of the instruments of husbandry; their maintenance is a circulating capital, in the same manner as that of the labouring servants. The farmer makes his profit by keeping the labouring cattle, and by parting with their maintenance. Both the price and the maintenance of the cattle which are bought in and fattened, not for labour, but for sale, are a circulating capital. The farmer makes his profit by parting with them. A flock of sheep or a herd of cattle, that, in a breeding country, is brought in neither for labour nor for sale, but in order to make a profit by their wool, by their milk, and by their increase, is a fixed capital. The profit is made by keeping them. Their maintenance is a circulating capital. The profit is made by parting with it; and it comes back with both its own profit and the profit upon the whole price of the cattle, in the price of the wool, the milk, and the increase. The whole value of the seed, too, is properly a fixed capital. Though it goes backwards and forwards between the ground and the granary, it never changes masters, and therefore does not properly circulate. The farmer makes his profit, not by its sale, but by its increase.
p9.zh: 农业工具中雇用的农民的首都部分是固定的,用于其劳动仆人的工资和维持是流通的资本。 他通过自己拥有它来谋取利益,而另一个则通过与它分离来谋取利益.其劳役牛的价格或价值为固定资本,其方式与畜牧工具相同;其维修为流通资本,其方式与劳役仆人相同.农夫通过养活劳役牛,与养殖分开来谋取利润.买入并肥大的牲畜的价格和维修,不是用来劳动的,而是用来出售的,都是流通资本。农民通过与他们分离来谋取利益.羊群或牛群,在繁育国,既不为劳役,也不为买卖而引进,而以羊毛,乳汁,增产牟利为固定之本.利润是通过保存它们而实现的。 他们的维修是流通资本.利润由分而成;既以自利,又以牛全价,以羊毛,牛奶,增价为主而得利.种子的全部价值也是适当的固定资本.虽在地与粮仓之间向后往前走,却从不改变主人,因此不适当地流通.农夫以利为主,不在于其买卖,而在于其增益.

p10.original: The general stock of any country or society is the same with that of all its inhabitants or members; and, therefore, naturally divides itself into the same three portions, each of which has a distinct function or office.
p10.zh: 任何国家或社会的总存量与其所有居民或成员相同;因此,自然地将自己分成三个相同的部分,每个部分都有不同的职能或职务。

p11.original: The first is that portion which is reserved for immediate consumption, and of which the characteristic is, that it affords no revenue or profit. It consists in the stock of food, clothes, household furniture, etc. which have been purchased by their proper consumers, but which are not yet entirely consumed. The whole stock of mere dwelling-houses, too, subsisting at anyone time in the country, make a part of this first portion. The stock that is laid out in a house, if it is to be the dwelling-house of the proprietor, ceases from that moment to serve in the function of a capital, or to afford any revenue to its owner. A dwelling-house, as such, contributes nothing to the revenue of its inhabitant; and though it is, no doubt, extremely useful to him, it is as his clothes and household furniture are useful to him, which, however, make a part of his expense, and not of his revenue. If it is to be let to a tenant for rent, as the house itself can produce nothing, the tenant must always pay the rent out of some other revenue, which he derives, either from labour, or stock, or land. Though a house, therefore, may yield a revenue to its proprietor, and thereby serve in the function of a capital to him, it cannot yield any to the public, nor serve in the function of a capital to it, and the revenue of the whole body of the people can never be in the smallest degree increased by it. Clothes and household furniture, in the same manner, sometimes yield a revenue, and thereby serve in the function of a capital to particular persons. In countries where masquerades are common, it is a trade to let out masquerade dresses for a night. Upholsterers frequently let furniture by the month or by the year. Undertakers let the furniture of funerals by the day and by the week. Many people let furnished houses, and get a rent, not only for the use of the house, but for that of the furniture. The revenue, however, which is derived from such things, must always be ultimately drawn from some other source of revenue. Of all parts of the stock, either of an individual or of a society, reserved for immediate consumption, what is laid out in houses is most slowly consumed. A stock of clothes may last several years; a stock of furniture half a century or a century; but a stock of houses, well built and properly taken care of, may last many centuries. Though the period of their total consumption, however, is more distant, they are still as really a stock reserved for immediate consumption as either clothes or household furniture.
p11.zh: 第一个是保留给立即消费的部分,其特点是,它不提供收入或利润。 它包括食品,衣服,家用家具等库存,这些库存已经由适当的消费者购买,但尚未完全消费.国内任何时间都存在的全部房屋,也构成第一部分的一部分。住房中的股票,如果是业主的住宅,则从那时起停止用于资本的功能,或支付所有者的任何收入。住宅本身对居民的收入没有任何贡献;虽然毫无疑问,这对他来说是极其有用的,但是,这是因为他的衣服和家庭家具对他是有用的,但是,这使他的开支成为一部分,而不是他的收入。 如果租户要租房,因为房屋本身无法生产,租户必须总是用他从劳力、库存或土地中获取的其他一些收入来支付租金。 因此,虽然房屋可能会给业主带来收入,从而为他发挥资本的作用,但它不能给公众带来任何收入,也不能为它发挥资本的作用,人民整体的收入永远不可能从它得到最小程度的增加。服装和家用家具,以同样的方式,有时产生收入,从而发挥特定个人的资本功能. 在化妆舞会很常见的国家,室内装潢者经常在月份或年份前让家具使用.殡葬者在白天和星期前让殡仪馆的家具使用.许多人让家具装修的房屋,并获得租金,不仅用于房屋使用,而且用于家具。 然而,这些物品产生的收入必须最终从其他一些收入来源中提取。无论是个人还是社会,在供直接消费的所有库存中,房屋中的物品消耗最慢。一套衣服可能持续数年;一套家具,半个世纪或一个世纪;但一套住房,建造良好和妥善处理,可能持续数个世纪。 然而,尽管他们的总消费期比较遥远,但是他们仍然像衣服或家用家具一样,是供立即消费的储备。

p12.original: The second of the three portions into which the general stock of the society divides itself, is the fixed capital; of which the characteristic is, that it affords a revenue or profit without circulating or changing masters. It consists chiefly of the four following articles.
p12.zh: 社会一般股分的三部分中的第二部分是固定资本;其特征是,它提供收入或利润而不流通或改变主人。 它主要由以下四条组成。

p13.original: First, of all useful machines and instruments of trade, which facilitate and abridge labour.
p13.zh: 第一,所有有用的贸易机器和工具,这些机器和工具便利和连接劳工。

p14.original: Secondly, of all those profitable buildings which are the means of procuring a revenue, not only to the proprietor who lets them for a rent, but to the person who possesses them, and pays that rent for them; such as shops, warehouses, work-houses, farm-houses, with all their necessary buildings, stables, granaries, etc. These are very different from mere dwelling-houses. They are a sort of instruments of trade, and may be considered in the same light.
p14.zh: 第二,在作为获取收入手段的所有盈利性建筑物中,不仅向让其出租的业主,而且向拥有者支付租金;例如商店、仓库、工作屋、农舍,以及所有必要的建筑物、马厩、粮仓等。 这些住房与单纯的住宅大不相同。 它们是一种贸易工具,可以从同样的角度加以考虑。

p15.original: Thirdly, of the improvements of land, of what has been profitably laid out in clearing, draining, inclosing, manuring, and reducing it into the condition most proper for tillage and culture. An improved farm may very justly be regarded in the same light as those useful machines which facilitate and abridge labour, and by means of which an equal circulating capital can afford a much greater revenue to its employer. An improved farm is equally advantageous and more durable than any of those machines, frequently requiring no other repairs than the most profitable application of the farmer's capital employed in cultivating it.
p15.zh: 第三,改善土地,改善在清理、排水、关闭、耕种和使土地成为最适于耕作和文化的条件方面已创造的有利条件。改善后的农场可以被公平看待,与那些便利和搭桥劳动的有用机器一样,通过这些机器,平等的流通资本可以为其雇主提供大得多的收入。改良的农场比任何一台机器都同样有利和耐用,往往不需要其他修理,只有最有利可图地利用农民用于耕作的资本。

p16.original: Fourthly, of the acquired and useful abilities of all the inhabitants and members of the society. The acquisition of such talents, by the maintenance of the acquirer during his education, study, or apprenticeship, always costs a real expense, which is a capital fixed and realized, as it were, in his person. Those talents, as they make a part of his fortune, so do they likewise that of the society to which he belongs. The improved dexterity of a workman may be considered in the same light as a machine or instrument of trade which facilitates and abridges labour, and which, though it costs a certain expense, repays that expense with a profit.
p16.zh: 第四,社会所有居民和成员获得的有用能力。获得者在教育、学习或学徒期间通过维持这种才能,总是要花费真正的费用,这是固定的资本,而且已经实现,就如他本人那样。 这些才华,因为他们是他财富的一部分,他们也是他所属社会的一部分。工人的德性提高,可以与便利和疏通劳动力、而且虽然花费一定费用但以利润偿还这种费用的机器或贸易工具一样,考虑得更加灵活。

p17.original: The third and last of the three portions into which the general stock of the society naturally divides itself, is the circulating capital, of which the characteristic is, that it affords a revenue only by circulating or changing masters. It is composed likewise of four parts.
p17.zh: 社会一般股票自然地分成三部分,其中第三部分也是最后一部分,是流通资本,其特点是,只有流通或更换主人才能提供收入。 它同样由四个部分组成。

p18.original: First, of the money, by means of which all the other three are circulated and distributed to their proper consumers.
p18.zh: 首先,通过这些钱,将其他三笔钱都分发给适当的消费者。

p19.original: Secondly, of the stock of provisions which are in the possession of the butcher, the grazier, the farmer, the corn-merchant, the brewer, etc. and from the sale of which they expect to derive a profit.
p19.zh: 第二,屠夫、格拉齐人、农民、玉米商、酿酒商等拥有的储备物资,以及他们期望从销售中获利的储备物资。

p20.original: Thirdly, of the materials, whether altogether rude, or more or less manufactured, of clothes, furniture, and building which are not yet made up into any of those three shapes, but which remain in the hands of the growers, the manufacturers, the mercers, and drapers, the timber-merchants, the carpenters and joiners, the brick-makers, etc.
p20.zh: 第三,无论是否完全粗鲁,或多或少制造,衣服,家具和建筑尚未组成这三种形状中的任何一种,但仍由种植者,制造商,商家,以及绘画家,木材商,木匠和参工,砖匠等掌握的材料.

p21.original: Fourthly, and lastly, of the work which is made up and completed, but which is still in the hands of the merchant and manufacturer, and not yet disposed of or distributed to the proper consumers; such as the finished work which we frequently find ready made in the shops of the smith, the cabinet-maker, the goldsmith, the jeweller, the china-merchant, etc. The circulating capital consists, in this manner, of the provisions, materials, and finished work of all kinds that are in the hands of their respective dealers, and of the money that is necessary for circulating and distributing them to those who are finally to use or to consume them.
p21.zh: 第四,也是最后一点,是那些编成和完成的,但仍在商家和制造商手中,尚未处理或分发给适当的消费者的作品;如我们经常发现的在匠家,柜家,金匠,珠宝商,瓷匠等商店中准备就绪的作品.流通资本以这种方式包括各自经销商手中的各种规定、材料和完成的工作,以及向最终使用或消费的人流通和分配这些物品所需的资金。

p22.original: Of these four parts, three--provisions, materials, and finished work, are either annually or in a longer or shorter period, regularly withdrawn from it, and placed either in the fixed capital, or in the stock reserved for immediate consumption.
p22.zh: 在这四个部分中,三供,材料,和竣工,每年或者在较长或者较短的时间内,定期退出,并放在固定资本中,或者放在预留供即时消费的库存中.

p23.original: Every fixed capital is both originally derived from, and requires to be continually supported by, a circulating capital. All useful machines and instruments of trade are originally derived from a circulating capital, which furnishes the materials of which they are made, and the maintenance of the workmen who make them. They require, too, a capital of the same kind to keep them in constant repair.
p23.zh: 每一种固定资本都最初来源于一种流通资本,需要这种资本不断支持。 所有有用的贸易机器和工具最初都来自流通资本,该资本提供制造这些机器和工具的材料,并维持制造这些机器和工具的工人。 它们也需要同一类的首都来保持它们不断的修复.

p24.original: No fixed capital can yield any revenue but by means of a circulating capital. The most useful machines and instruments of trade will produce nothing, without the circulating capital, which affords the materials they are employed upon, and the maintenance of the workmen who employ them. Land, however improved, will yield no revenue without a circulating capital, which maintains the labourers who cultivate and collect its produce.
p24.zh: 任何固定资本都无法产生任何收入,只能通过流通资本。 最有用的贸易机器和工具将一无所有,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本的工人的维持,没有流通资本和工具,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有流通资本,没有能够提供他们所使用的材料。 无论土地情况如何改善,如果没有流通资本,维持耕种和收割其农产品的劳工,就不会产生任何收入。

p25.original: To maintain and augment the stock which maybe reserved for immediate consumption, is the sole end and purpose both of the fixed and circulating capitals. It is this stock which feeds, clothes, and lodges the people. Their riches or poverty depend upon the abundant or sparing supplies which those two capitals can afford to the stock reserved for immediate consumption.
p25.zh: 维持和增加可能留给立即消费的库存,是固定和流通首都的唯一目的。食物、衣服和住宿都是这种股票的产物。它们的财富或贫穷取决于这两个首都能够负担的供立即消费的储备的充足或闲置供应。

p26.original: So great a part of the circulating capital being continually withdrawn from it, in order to be placed in the other two branches of the general stock of the society, it must in its turn require continual supplies without which it would soon cease to exist. These supplies are principally drawn from three sources; the produce of land, of mines, and of fisheries. These afford continual supplies of provisions and materials, of which part is afterwards wrought up into finished work and by which are replaced the provisions, materials, and finished work, continually withdrawn from the circulating capital. From mines, too, is drawn what is necessary for maintaining and augmenting that part of it which consists in money. For though, in the ordinary course of business, this part is not, like the other three, necessarily withdrawn from it, in order to be placed in the other two branches of the general stock of the society, it must, however, like all other things, be wasted and worn out at last, and sometimes, too, be either lost or sent abroad, and must, therefore, require continual, though no doubt much smaller supplies.
p26.zh: 如此大一部分流通资本不断被从中抽走,为了被投入到社会总存量的另外两个分支,它就必须需要持续的供给,没有这种供给,它将很快不复存在。 这些供应品主要来自三个方面:土地、矿山和渔业。 这些用品和材料持续供应,其中一部分随后被编成完成的工作,并用这些用品、材料和完成的工作来取代,这些用品和材料继续从流通资本中撤出。 从地雷中也提取了维持和增加其中资金部分所需的资金。 然而,在正常的经营过程中,这一部分不一定像其他三个部分一样,必然从这一部分中撤走,为了被放在社会一般储备的另外两个分支中,它必须像所有其他事物一样,最终被浪费和磨损,有时也会丢失或送往国外,因此,必须不断需要供应,尽管毫无疑问,供应量要小得多。

p27.original: Lands, mines, and fisheries, require all both a fixed and circulating capital to cultivate them; and their produce replaces, with a profit not only those capitals, but all the others in the society. Thus the farmer annually replaces to the manufacturer the provisions which he had consumed, and the materials which he had wrought up the year before; and the manufacturer replaces to the farmer the finished work which he had wasted and worn out in the same time. This is the real exchange that is annually made between those two orders of people, though it seldom happens that the rude produce of the one, and the manufactured produce of the other, are directly bartered for one another; because it seldom happens that the farmer sells his corn and his cattle, his flax and his wool, to the very same person of whom he chuses to purchase the clothes, furniture, and instruments of trade, which he wants. He sells, therefore, his rude produce for money, with which he can purchase, wherever it is to be had, the manufactured produce he has occasion for. Land even replaces, in part at least, the capitals with which fisheries and mines are cultivated. It is the produce of land which draws the fish from the waters; and it is the produce of the surface of the earth which extracts the minerals from its bowels.
p27.zh: 土地、矿山和渔业需要所有固定和流通的资本来耕种;他们的产品不仅可以用来取代这些首都,而且可以用来取代社会中的所有其他国家。 因此,农民每年将他消费的物品和他前一年制造的材料更换给制造商;制造商将他同时浪费和磨损的已完成的工作更换给农民。 这是每年这两类人之间的真正交换,尽管很少发生一个粗鲁的农产品和另一个的制成品直接相互交换;因为农民很少将他的玉米和牛、他的麻和羊毛卖给他要购买的衣服、家具和交易工具的同一个人。 因此,他出售他粗鲁的农产品以换取金钱,他可以用这些产品购买,而无论它在哪里得到,他所要购买的制成品。土地甚至至少部分地取代了种植渔业和矿山的首都。 是土地的产物把鱼从水中引出;是地表的产物从肠道中提取矿物。

p28.original: The produce of land, mines, and fisheries, when their natural fertility is equal, is in proportion to the extent and proper application of the capitals employed about them. When the capitals are equal, and equally well applied, it is in proportion to their natural fertility.
p28.zh: 土地、矿山和渔业的产量,如果其自然肥力相等,则与所雇用的首都的比例相称。 当首都是平等的,而且同样适用得当时,这与其自然生育率成正比。

p29.original: In all countries where there is a tolerable security, every man of common understanding will endeavour to employ whatever stock he can command, in procuring either present enjoyment or future profit. If it is employed in procuring present enjoyment, it is a stock reserved for immediate consumption. If it is employed in procuring future profit, it must procure this profit either by staying with him, or by going from him. In the one case it is a fixed, in the other it is a circulating capital. A man must be perfectly crazy, who, where there is a tolerable security, does not employ all the stock which he commands, whether it be his own, or borrowed of other people, in some one or other of those three ways.
p29.zh: 在有可容忍的安全保障的所有国家,每个具有共同理解的人将努力利用他能够掌握的任何库存来获得目前的享受或未来的利润。 如果它被用于获取现成的享受,它就是供立即消费的储备。 如果它受雇于争取未来的利润,它就必须通过留在他身边或从他那里获得这种利润。 在一种情况下,它是固定的,在另一种情况下,是流通的资本。一个人一定是完全疯狂的,在有可容忍的担保的情况下,他并不使用他所指挥的所有股票,无论是他自己,还是借给其他人的,都以这三种方式中的某种方式或另一种方式.

p30.original: In those unfortunate countries, indeed, where men are continually afraid of the violence of their superiors, they frequently bury or conceal a great part of their stock, in order to have it always at hand to carry with them to some place of safety, in case of their being threatened with any of those disasters to which they consider themselves at all times exposed. This is said to be a common practice in Turkey, in Indostan, and, I believe, in most other governments of Asia. It seems to have been a common practice among our ancestors during the violence of the feudal government. Treasure-trove was, in these times, considered as no contemptible part of the revenue of the greatest sovereigns in Europe. It consisted in such treasure as was found concealed in the earth, and to which no particular person could prove any right. This was regarded, in those times, as so important an object, that it was always considered as belonging to the sovereign, and neither to the finder nor to the proprietor of the land, unless the right to it had been conveyed to the latter by an express clause in his charter. It was put upon the same footing with gold and silver mines, which, without a special clause in the charter, were never supposed to be comprehended in the general grant of the lands, though mines of lead, copper, tin, and coal were, as things of smaller consequence.
p30.zh: 在那些不幸的国家里,人们一直害怕上司的暴力,他们经常埋藏或隐藏着他们大部分的库存,以便永远能够携带他们到安全的地方,以防他们随时受到他们认为自己会遭受的任何灾难的威胁。 据说,这是土耳其、印度斯坦和我相信亚洲大多数其他国家政府的普遍做法。 在封建政府的暴力期间,这似乎一直是我们祖先中的一种普遍做法.宝藏在这些时代被认为是欧洲最伟大的主权者收入中不可轻视的部分. 它包含在隐藏在地球上的宝藏中,没有任何特定的人能够证明它有任何权利。 在那些时候,这被视为一个如此重要的目标,因此,它始终被认为是属于君主的,而不是属于土地的发现者或拥有者,除非其宪章中的一项明文条款向后者传达了对土地的权利。 它与金矿和银矿处于同样的地位,尽管铅矿、铜矿、锡矿和煤矿的后果较小,但是在宪章中没有特别条款,这些金矿和银矿不应该被理解为土地的一般赠与。
